title: Rename and relink
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for renaming products, repositories and pages and rewriting every reference and link to the new names: an inventory of every spelling at exact commits, rewrites in local copies, link checks that rely on no redirect, the owner's host renames on the record, a sweep that decides clean, and a plain notice for each retired address.
boundaries: Workers read local copies, edit local copies and check links read-only. Renaming on hosts, landing rewrites and showing notices are the owner's acts.
No redirect is relied on. Old names stay only in named allowed contexts such as provenance and history.
Names that must never be written down are searched by hash, never spelled out in a noun.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for renaming products, repositories and pages and rewriting every reference to the new names

value.lets_workers: Turn a rename decision into a map, inventory every spelling of every old name across exact commits, plan and make the rewrites in local copies, check every link without relying on redirects, have the owner record the renames only they can do on hosts, sweep until no old name remains outside an allowed context, and draft a plain notice for each retired address.

flow.when: As soon as a rename map is decided.
From the inventory; the owner's host acts are listed separately.
Per repository, in a local copy.
When the owner has renamed repositories, sites or addresses on their hosts.
After rewrites and host renames, and again before calling the rename done.
Last; it decides clean or not.
For each retired address that will keep showing something.

guardrails: No redirect is relied on: every link points at the new address directly.
Old names stay only in named allowed contexts such as provenance and history.
Renaming on hosts is the owner's act; workers edit local copies and check.

nouns.title: How a rename reaches every reference
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: A person decides the rename map: old and new names, addresses and where old names may stay.
build-inventory finds every variant of every old name at exact commits.
plan-rewrites groups edits per file and lists what only a person can change.
rewrite-references edits local copies and runs each repository's own checks.
The owner renames repositories, sites and addresses on their hosts and records it with record-host-renames.
check-links resolves every link and records redirects and failures.
sweep-old-names decides clean or not; write-archive-notice drafts what old addresses say.
rules: Status lines, commit messages for new work, captions and alt text count; history and receipts do not change.
A redirect that happens to work is still a violation of a clean rename.
Text inside images and videos goes to a person; workers list it, never guess it.
A name that keeps coming back is a finding with a guard, not another sweep.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

verbs.title: Inventory every reference to the old names
verbs.summary: Expand every old name into its variants and find each occurrence in local copies at exact commits, by reference type.
verbs.outcome: A reference inventory, with places outside the repositories listed separately.

slots.name: rename_map
slots.description: Pin of the decided rename map.

slots.name: repositories
slots.description: Pins of the local repository copies at exact commits.

steps: Expand each old name with the variant rules before searching.
Search every file in each copy, including docs, configuration, workflows and tests, and record repository, file, line, variant and reference type.
List text inside images and videos, and places outside the repositories, for a person instead of guessing them.

acceptance.check: The inventory validates against template.reference-inventory's schema.
Every repository is recorded with the commit that was searched.
Rerunning the search at the same commits yields the same occurrences.

network: Reads local copies only; no request leaves the machine.

verbs.title: Plan the rewrites
verbs.summary: Group the inventory into edits per file, mark what stays under an allowed context, and list what only a person or the owner can change.
verbs.outcome: A rewrite plan covering every occurrence.
steps: Make every occurrence either an edit or a keep with its allowed context.
Point every link at the new address directly; never plan a redirect as the fix.
List host renames as owner acts, in order, and text in media as items for a person.

acceptance.check: The plan validates against template.rewrite-plan's schema.
The edit and keep counts add up to the inventory's occurrences.
No planned change relies on a redirect.

verbs.title: Rewrite references in a local copy
verbs.summary: Make the planned edits for one repository in a local copy and run that repository's own checks.
verbs.outcome: A rewrite held as a patch with its check results; nothing leaves the local copy.

slots.name: repository
slots.description: Pin of the local repository copy.

steps: Apply only the planned edits for this repository; leave history and allowed contexts untouched.
Run the repository's own checks and record each command, exit code and summary.
Hold the result as a patch with its digest. Never push it; landing it is the owner's release.

acceptance.check: The rewrite validates against template.rewrite's schema.
The patch applies cleanly to base_commit.
Every check command has a recorded exit code.

network: Package installs inside the sandbox to run the repository's own checks; no requests to any live system.

verbs.title: Record the renames carried out on hosts
verbs.summary: The owner records each rename they carried out on a host, with the old address, the new address and when. This template performs nothing itself.
verbs.outcome: A host rename record, with any renames still pending.

slots.name: rewrite_plan
slots.description: Pin of the rewrite plan listing the owner acts.

steps: Write each old and new address exactly as the host shows it.
List any planned host rename not yet carried out under not_done.

acceptance.check: The record validates against template.host-rename-record's schema.
Every owner act in the plan appears in renames or not_done.

verbs.title: Check every link
verbs.summary: Resolve every link in the rewritten files and record which ones reach their target directly, which redirect and which fail.
verbs.outcome: A link check with redirects and failures listed.

slots.name: rewrites
slots.description: Pins of the rewrites or repository copies to check.

steps: Collect every absolute and relative link from the rewritten files.
Resolve relative links inside the repository; request absolute links read-only and record any redirect with its final address.
List links to places the team does not control under outside_control.

acceptance.check: The link check validates against template.link-check's schema.
ok plus redirected plus broken equals checked.

network: Read-only requests to each absolute link in the rewritten files; no forms are submitted and nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Sweep for old names and decide clean
verbs.summary: Search the final local copies for every variant of every old name, combine the link check and host rename record, and decide whether the rename is clean.
verbs.outcome: An old-name sweep that passes the rename checks, with verdict clean, violations_found or unknown.

slots.name: repositories
slots.description: Pins of the final local copies at exact commits.

slots.name: link_check
slots.description: Pin of the latest link check.

slots.name: host_rename_record
slots.description: Pin of the owner's host rename record.

steps: Search with every variant; record each hit as a violation or an allowed hit with its context.
Copy redirects and broken links from the link check, and host renames from the owner's record.
Write clean only when there are no violations, no redirects and no broken links; propose record-finding for each violation.

acceptance.check: The sweep validates against template.old-name-sweep's schema.
The sweep passes the pinned rename checks.
Rerunning the search at the same commits yields the same hits.

network: Reads local copies and pinned nouns only; no request leaves the machine.

verbs.title: Draft the notice for a retired address
verbs.summary: Draft a short, plain notice for a retired address: the new name and address, what moved, what did not and that it will not forward.
verbs.outcome: An archive notice draft; the owner decides where and when it appears.

retired_name.description: The retired name whose old address shows the notice.

steps: Lead with the new name and the new address.
Say plainly that the old address will not forward, and list what stayed behind.
Keep it under 1,200 characters, in plain words.

acceptance.check: The notice validates against template.archive-notice's schema.
A reader new to the project understands where to go.
